description: Raise a named interrupt, and wrap the call in two nested handlers that disagree. Tests the raise/raises/handle syntax and the rule that every handler in the chain runs, and any rejection wins.

input.assignment: Write a module that exports two functions. First, `archiveNotes(count: number): Result<string>`: before doing anything it raises an interrupt with the effect name `notes::archive`, carrying `count` in the interrupt's data. If the interrupt is approved, it returns success("archived ${count}"). Second, `runArchive(count: number): string`. This function calls archiveNotes inside an inner handler that approves `notes::archive`, but that inner handler sits inside an outer handler. The outer handler rejects `notes::archive` when the count is greater than 10, and passes on it otherwise. runArchive returns "archived" when archiveNotes succeeded and "rejected" when it was rejected. Above runArchive, write a doc comment that says, for count = 11, which of the two handlers run, what runArchive returns, and why.
